event.summary: removed terminal capability fields are fenced by protocol skew
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: considered whether supervisor replies that no longer report terminal kinds could make an older client select the wrong attachment behavior or hide required migration controls. Source analysis: the same commit removes agent_terminal and supervisor_creates_host_terminals from farhelm-proto::SessionInfo and bumps PROTOCOL_VERSION from 76 to 77 (farhelm-proto/src/lib.rs:255). SPEC_impl.md, Version and skew, requires incompatible peers to refuse at hello and explicitly says omission that changes receiver behavior needs a bump. The core patch removes only construction/projection of those removed members; the revision supports terminal hosts only. Suggested bucket: other (refuted compatibility defect). Confidence: confirmed from source, no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation, protocol bump fences old live peers; this does not rely on accepting a dangerous behavior in the specification. Could-be-highest: no security or loss-of-work route established for these reply fields. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Caveat: this checks the assigned reply-field removal and adjacent protocol contract, not all grid-only transport changes in the commit.

event.summary: removed terminal capability fields are fenced by protocol skew
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: original potential consequence retained: removing terminal-kind replies could send an older client down the wrong attachment path or hide migration controls. Suggested bucket: other; no established defect or loss-of-work route. Confidence: confirmed source refutation for the assigned field removal, no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation. Same-commit farhelm-proto/src/lib.rs:255 bumps protocol 76 to 77; io.rs:629 accepts only exact protocol equality, otherwise returns structured VersionSkew. This is an implementation fence, not merely a specification acceptance. Synthesis checked the second path through persisted listings: SessionInfo and TabInfo tolerate unknown old JSON keys; the existing test a_session_cached_with_terminal_kinds_still_decodes (lib.rs:7449-7508) asserts omission on serialization and successful decode with both removed members and mixed old tab kinds. No live consumer of either removed member remains in supervisor/helm/UI source (targeted git grep; other agent_terminal matches name functions, not members). service/terminals.rs:225-283 resolves Attach from the actual entry's HostTerminal or refuses a missing terminal; it does not infer a terminal from SessionInfo. Helm terminal.rs:40-68 relays only grids and documents the live handshake fence; its query no longer chooses a stream kind. core.rs:11820-11862 still publishes before projecting checkout metadata and keeps the accepted session ID in an error after publication. Therefore field omission is neither a host-readiness oracle nor a replacement for the actual Attach resolution. Could-be-highest: no route established; a wrongly selected display path alone does not establish destructive action or lost user work. possible_cover: none. Caveats: this is not an audit of all grid transport, UI bootstrap, cached-host connection policy or old-terminal retirement changes; no parent drop accepted, retain for independent disposition. Source conclusions only; existing test read, not executed.

event.summary: reload test waits for the host exit observation boundary
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 70bc66a9f285cc2a9984924f389834d118b7cfdc. TLDR: considered whether observing exits after reload weakened the pending-Stop regression test by manufacturing the desired outcome. Source analysis: core.rs:39905-40023 first adopts the real host and waits for its exit, asserts the competing wrapper/preparation inference applies, and durably records StopRequested. release_fixture_host aborts only that runtime before reload; observe_reloaded_host_exits at 40046 waits for each returned host runtime to read Exited and invokes the shipped ticker observer with those entries. The changed test at 40101-40152 also asserts the host is found exactly in the non-absent case. SPEC_impl.md:2678-2685 says an offline child's exit reads as running until replay, after which the ticker records the exit, and reload leaves a durable Stop request intact for that case. This matches the actual boundary rather than bypassing it. Suggested bucket: other (no established test defect). Confidence: confirmed from source, no execution. proposed_drop: source and contract refutation; the helper uses the production observer after the documented exit replay boundary. Could-be-highest: no shipped data-loss or security route established; this concern was about regression-test strength. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Caveat: source review does not show a runtime pass.

event.summary: reload test waits for the host exit observation boundary
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 70bc66a9f285cc2a9984924f389834d118b7cfdc. TLDR: original concern retained: a test that completes reload with a manufactured observation could conceal a lost pending-Stop annotation or incorrect startup error. Suggested bucket: other for this test-strength concern, no established shipped defect. Confidence: confirmed source refutation of the oracle concern, no execution. proposed_drop: source and contract refutation. Synthesis checks of readiness and teardown: pending_startup_stop_fixture:39905-40023 waits for the actual host exit, verifies dead owned evidence and the competing wrapper/preparation inference before durably storing StopRequested. The reload test:40101-40152 ends the host through shutdown and asserts ended plus empty sockets in the absent case, or aborts only its runtime in the present case; it asserts terminal presence matches that choice. hosts/terminal.rs:2398 abort cancels the runtime task and encodes, without a host shutdown; a recovered runtime then reads the host's actual journal. on_exited at 3814-3823 flushes/publishes emulator state before setting Liveness::Exited, so wait_for_host_exit establishes processed exit rather than mere process disappearance. core/tests/host_terminals.rs:73-93 subscribes before checking, bounds the wait, and prints current status on failure. observe_reloaded_host_exits:40046 calls the production ticker observer on returned entries, not synthetic terminal evidence. Production ticker.rs:1211-1240 selects Running/StopRequested host entries with Owned dead evidence and calls the same observer; core.rs:7586 leaves StopRequested while reaped-child replay is incomplete, and status.rs:871/894 suppresses only inferred failures. Thus those entries satisfy the caller's observation readiness. The helper deliberately does not exercise ticker scheduling or installation of the returned reload map; that is a limit of this classification test, not evidence it claims those boundaries. StateDir wraps TestDir; teststate/lib.rs:794-808 ends remaining hosts before deleting their socket directory and keeps the directory if shutdown cannot be confirmed. Diagnostics remain within the live fixture. Could-be-highest: no security or user-work-loss route established for this oracle concern. possible_cover: none. Caveats: source-only; no runtime pass, scheduling coverage or full teardown correctness claimed. No parent drop accepted; retain for independent disposition.

event.summary: borrower reload test may keep a competing origin runtime attached
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 70bc66a9f285cc2a9984924f389834d118b7cfdc. TLDR: the borrower case of checkout_interruption_status_matches_reload may run reload while the original checkout session's host runtime is still attached, permitting two runtimes to contend for the same host instead of modeling a restarted supervisor. Source basis: core.rs:41773-41800 creates a live origin with long_lived_launcher, then creates a borrower; :41857-41862 shuts down only the selected borrower's host, and :41879 reloads all sessions without releasing the origin runtime. Earlier assigned fixture documentation at 39729-39734 explicitly warns that two runtimes keep taking a host over, and release_fixture_host handles that boundary in the pending-Stop tests. Need source checks: determine whether reload automatically keeps/skips this live origin's runtime through a global registry or whether this wrapper scans/adopts it; check ownership and lifetime of the original origin runtime through reload and test return. Exact missing premise: whether this test actually creates a second owning runtime for the still-live origin rather than preserving the existing one, and whether that affects the tested borrower oracle or solely leaves a bad fixture premise. Suspected consequence is test reliability/lifecycle validity, not production data loss. Suggested bucket: other pending checks. Confidence: concrete source lead, no execution. Could-be-highest: no established security or user-work-loss route. proposed_drop: false pending source investigation. possible_cover: none in supplied neighbour findings; not c3's already-released pending-Stop fixture. No reproduction or runtime test.

event.summary: borrower reload creates competing runtimes for its live origin
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 70bc66a9f285cc2a9984924f389834d118b7cfdc. Original suspected consequence retained: the borrower case may contend for its origin host and weaken reload-fixture validity or reliability. Source checks establish the ownership premise: test wrapper reload_sessions at 7957-7978 explicitly supplies an empty adopted map and tabs with no notifier; attribute_host_rows (core/host_handover.rs:672-710) skips only supplied adopted hosts, then scans/takes over and adopts pending rows (736-790). The original supervisor still holds the live origin handle, so a second runtime is created for that origin. terminal.rs:3964-4040 reconnects when a connection is taken over, until the bounded reconnect limit or handles disappear; there is no automatic global reuse. However the test asserts only the stopped borrower's classification, not the origin's post-reload liveness, so contention alone does not establish failure of its asserted result. A separate exact documentation discrepancy is now visible: wrapper doc at 7961 says The tests that use it have no hosts, while the assigned migration explicitly calls it with hosts, including the origin not shut down in the borrower case. Need check attribution across the full pinned range and later state, then retain only the supported consequence, not a conjectured flake. Suggested bucket: other. Confidence: source-confirmed competing runtime and stale helper assumption; no execution, no observed failing schedule. Could-be-highest: no. proposed_drop: false while attribution and distinction are checked. possible_cover: no matching item in supplied neighbour context; not the known exit-oracle c3. Exact remaining premise for a test-failure claim: a dependency from origin contention to the selected borrower's asserted result; the inspected code has not supplied one.

event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 70bc66a9f285cc2a9984924f389834d118b7cfdc. TLDR: the converted checkout-status test reloads a still-running origin host while its original runtime is attached. The test creates two owners that can take the same host back from each other, rather than modeling a restarted supervisor. The supported finding is an unintended fixture ownership conflict and inaccurate helper assumption, not an observed flaky assertion or production failure. Suggested bucket: other (test fixture/lifecycle validity). Confidence: confirmed by source/caller ownership analysis, no execution. proposed_drop: false. Could-be-highest: no established security or user-work-loss route. possible_cover: none in the supplied exact neighbour records; no prohibited coverage sources searched.

Source: checkout_interruption_status_matches_reload creates a live origin using long_lived_launcher at core.rs:41773-41780. In the borrower branch :41793-41799 it creates another session and selects that borrower's info; the supervisor's session map still owns the origin runtime. :41857-41862 ends only the selected borrower's host. :41879 invokes reload_sessions over all rows, without aborting or passing the live origin handle. This wrapper at :7957-7978 supplies adopted: HashMap::new() and tabs: HashMap::new(); its comment explicitly states no runtime counts as already adopted and incorrectly still says The tests that use it have no hosts. attribute_host_rows in core/host_handover.rs:672-710 skips only passed adopted/tab sockets, scans with HostRegistry, and at :764-790 adopts the origin over the scan's connection. Registry scan calls HostConnection::connect_with at hosts/registry.rs:775; client.rs:1277-1279 always sends take_over: true. The original handle remains in sup.sessions. hosts/terminal.rs:3964-4040 reconnects on takeover while its control channel is open, up to its bounded instability limit. Thus no global registry or handle drop silently prevents the second owner. The host contract at SPEC_impl.md:2077-2078 says Each host has one owning connection inside the supervisor, since a second connection takes the host over from the first without notice. The same commit's helper docs at core.rs:39729-39734 explicitly warn about two runtimes taking over and require abort before another reload.

Attribution and limits: the range base 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a's corresponding test (:41488 onward) uses tmux_supervisor; this origin has no reconnecting host runtime. The immediate parent has the same tmux fixture. The assigned migration introduces the still-live competing host owner in this test. The no-hosts wrapper comment predates the range (git log -S found no introduction inside the complete range); this finding does not claim that old comment itself was newly authored. The new caller violates its stated assumption, just as it begins making the stale claim false for this caller. Production reload already supports preserving existing runtimes via its adopted map; this test wrapper passes none.

Original potential consequence preserved and narrowed after investigation: origin takeover could affect test reliability or make the reload fixture unrepresentative. The test checks only the stopped borrower's result, so source has not established that contention changes those assertions. Do not label this a confirmed flake, fabricate a failure trace, or claim the borrower is misclassified. Neither current correct borrower classification nor that limitation removes the concrete second-owner setup. Fix direction: release the origin's runtime before the manual reload (or pass the existing runtime deliberately), and document the wrapper's ownership requirement. Keep the selected borrower's stopped/absent boundary unchanged. No reproduction, runtime test, build or live-install operation.
